title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 20. The Play in the Gundicha Temple
html:
The Lord asks Damodara Pandita about His mother's devotion; the bathing festival, the anavasara and the journey to Alalanatha; the Ratha-yatra: in the mood of Radha the Lord leads Jagannatha to Gundicha as to Vrindavana

Verse 1

एकदा पृष्टवान् कृष्णः श्रीदामोदरपण्डितम्।
सत्यं कथय मन्मातुः कृष्णभक्तिर्दृढास्ति किम्॥१॥

ekadā pṛṣṭavān kṛṣṇaḥ śrīdāmodarapaṇḍitam|
satyaṁ kathaya manmātuḥ kṛṣṇabhaktirdṛḍhāsti kim||1||

ekada — once; prishtavan — asked; krishnah — Krishna; shri-damodara-panditam — Sri Damodara Pandita; satyam — truly; kathaya — tell; mat-matuh — of My mother; krishna-bhaktih — devotion to Krishna; dridha — firm; asti — is; kim — whether.

1Once Krishna1 asked Sri Damodara Pandita, "Tell Me truly: is My mother's devotion to Krishna firm?"

Verse 2

श्रुत्वा स प्राह सक्रोधस्तत्प्रसादात् परं त्वयि।
सास्ति कृष्णरसा भक्तिर्नित्यानन्दस्वरूपिणी॥२॥

śrutvā sa prāha sakrodhastatprasādāt paraṁ tvayi|
sāsti kṛṣṇarasā bhaktirnityānandasvarūpiṇī||2||

shrutva — hearing; sah — he; praha — said; sa-krodhah — angrily; tat-prasadat — by her grace; param — alone; tvayi — in You; sa — that; asti — is; krishna-rasa — full of the rasa of Krishna; bhaktih — devotion; nitya-ananda-svarupini — whose nature is eternal bliss.

2Hearing this, he answered angrily, "It is only by her grace that there is in You that devotion, full of the rasa of Krishna, whose nature is eternal bliss!"

Verse 3

श्रुत्वा विप्रं परिष्वज्य प्राह सकरुणं प्रभुः।
यथा त्वं प्राह मां बन्धो सत्यं तत्सर्वमेव हि॥३॥

śrutvā vipraṁ pariṣvajya prāha sakaruṇaṁ prabhuḥ|
yathā tvaṁ prāha māṁ bandho satyaṁ tatsarvameva hi||3||

shrutva — hearing; vipram — the brahmana; parishvajya — embracing; praha — said; sa-karunam — tenderly; prabhuh — the Lord; yatha — as; tvam — you; praha — said; mam — to Me; bandho — O friend; satyam — true; tat — that; sarvam — all; eva hi — indeed.

3Hearing this, the Lord tenderly embraced the brahmana and said, "My friend, all that you have said to Me is true.

Verse 4

तदाज्ञया हि क्षेत्रेऽस्मिन् वसामि नात्र संशयः।
तत्प्रेम्णा नीयते तस्याः सन्निधिमप्यलं खलु॥४॥

tadājñayā hi kṣetre'smin vasāmi nātra saṁśayaḥ|
tatpremṇā nīyate tasyāḥ sannidhimapyalaṁ khalu||4||

tat-ajnaya — by her command; hi — for; kshetre asmin — in this Kshetra; vasami — I dwell; na atra samshayah — there is no doubt of it; tat-premna — by her love; niyate — (I) am drawn; tasyah — to her; sannidhim — into the presence; api — yet; alam — fully; khalu — truly.

4It is only by her command that I live in this Kshetra, of that there is no doubt — and yet her love draws Me back to her again and again."

Verse 5

ततः श्रीजगदीशस्य स्नानयात्रामहोत्सवम्।
ददर्श परमप्रीतः सभक्तः साग्रजो हरिः॥५॥

tataḥ śrījagadīśasya snānayātrāmahotsavam|
dadarśa paramaprītaḥ sabhaktaḥ sāgrajo hariḥ||5||

tatah — then; shri-jagadishasya — of Sri Jagadisha (Jagannatha); snana-yatra-maha-utsavam — the great festival of the bathing; dadarsha — beheld; parama-pritah — with great joy; sa-bhaktah — with His devotees; sa-agrajah — with His elder brother; harih — Hari.

5Then Hari, with His devotees and His elder brother, beheld in great joy the great bathing festival2 of Sri Jagadisha.

Verse 6

ततोऽनवसरं वीक्ष्य राममाधवयोः प्रभुः।
सभक्तो दुःखसंतप्तो गत्वाप्यालालनाथकम्॥६॥

tato'navasaraṁ vīkṣya rāmamādhavayoḥ prabhuḥ|
sabhakto duḥkhasaṁtapto gatvāpyālālanāthakam||6||

tatah — then; anavasaram — the anavasara (the period when the Lord is not seen); vikshya — seeing; rama-madhavayoh — of Rama and Madhava; prabhuh — the Lord; sa-bhaktah — with His devotees; duhkha-santaptah — tormented by grief; gatva — going; api — also; alalanathakam — to Alalanatha.

6Afterwards, seeing that the anavasara3 of Rama and Madhava had come, the Lord, tormented by grief, went with His devotees to Alalanatha4;

Verse 7

पश्यन् देवं सप्तरात्रं स्थित्वायातः स सत्वरम्।
नेत्रोत्सवं च संपश्यन् साग्रजस्य जगत्पतेः॥७॥

paśyan devaṁ saptarātraṁ sthitvāyātaḥ sa satvaram|
netrotsavaṁ ca saṁpaśyan sāgrajasya jagatpateḥ||7||

pashyan — beholding; devam — the Lord; sapta-ratram — for seven nights; sthitva — staying; ayatah — returned; sah — He; satvaram — quickly; netra-utsavam — the festival of the eyes (Netrotsava); cha — and; sampashyan — beholding; sa-agrajasya — with His elder brother; jagat-pateh — of the Lord of the world.

7beholding the Lord there, He stayed seven nights, and then hastened back to see the Netrotsava5 of the Lord of the world and His elder brother.

Verse 8

संकीर्तनरसानन्दैर्ननर्त स्वजनैः सह।
भक्ताभिमानी भगवान् नित्यानन्दकराश्रितः॥८॥

saṁkīrtanarasānandairnanarta svajanaiḥ saha|
bhaktābhimānī bhagavān nityānandakarāśritaḥ||8||

sankirtana-rasa-anandaih — in the bliss of the rasa of sankirtana; nanarta — danced; sva-janaih saha — with His own people; bhakta-abhimani — who regards Himself as a devotee; bhagavan — the Lord; nityananda-kara-ashritah — holding Nityananda's hand.

8The Lord, who regards Himself as a devotee, holding Nityananda's hand, danced with His own people in the bliss of the rasa of sankirtana.

Verse 9

ततः स्वमालयं गत्वा स्वभक्तैः संवृतो हरिः।
भुक्त्वा महाप्रसादं च भक्तदत्तं सुखं बभौ॥९॥

tataḥ svamālayaṁ gatvā svabhaktaiḥ saṁvṛto hariḥ|
bhuktvā mahāprasādaṁ ca bhaktadattaṁ sukhaṁ babhau||9||

tatah — then; svam — to His own; alayam — dwelling; gatva — going; sva-bhaktaih — by His devotees; samvritah — surrounded; harih — Hari; bhuktva — partaking of; maha-prasadam — the mahaprasada; cha — and; bhakta-dattam — given by the devotees; sukham — happily; babhau — shone.

9Then, coming to His own dwelling surrounded by His devotees, Hari partook of the mahaprasada given by the devotees and shone with happiness.

Verse 10

एवं सदानन्दरसेऽतिमत्तः
श्रीगौरचन्द्रो हरिरामयोः शुभम्।
महाविभूत्योः किल स्यन्दनोत्सवं
द्रष्टुं स्वभक्तैः सह सत्वरं ययौ॥१०॥

evaṁ sadānandarase'timattaḥ
śrīgauracandro harirāmayoḥ śubham|
mahāvibhūtyoḥ kila syandanotsavaṁ
draṣṭuṁ svabhaktaiḥ saha satvaraṁ yayau||10||

evam — thus; sada-ananda-rase — in the rasa of eternal bliss; ati-mattah — deeply intoxicated; shri-gaurachandrah — Sri Gaurachandra; hari-ramayoh — of Hari and Rama; shubham — auspicious; maha-vibhutyoh — of great majesty; kila — indeed; syandana-utsavam — the chariot festival; drashtum — to see; sva-bhaktaih saha — with His devotees; satvaram — quickly; yayau — went.

10Thus Sri Gaurachandra, deeply intoxicated with the rasa of eternal bliss, hastened with His devotees to see the auspicious chariot festival of Hari and Rama, full of great majesty.

Verse 11

दृष्ट्वा च रामं मधुसूदनं च
सुदर्शनेनापि युतां सुभद्राम्।
रथस्थितौ तौ रथसंस्थितां तां
संवीक्ष्य हर्षेण ननाम साग्रजः॥११॥

dṛṣṭvā ca rāmaṁ madhusūdanaṁ ca
sudarśanenāpi yutāṁ subhadrām|
rathasthitau tau rathasaṁsthitāṁ tāṁ
saṁvīkṣya harṣeṇa nanāma sāgrajaḥ||11||

drishtva — seeing; cha — and; ramam — Rama; madhusudanam — Madhusudana; cha — and; sudarshanena — with Sudarshana; api — also; yutam — together; subhadram — Subhadra; ratha-sthitau — standing on their chariots; tau — the two; ratha-samsthitam — standing on her chariot; tam — her; samvikshya — beholding; harshena — joyfully; nanama — bowed; sa-agrajah — with His elder brother.

11Seeing Rama and Madhusudana, and Subhadra together with Sudarshana6 — the two standing on Their chariots and her standing on her chariot — He joyfully bowed to them together with His elder brother.

Verse 12

श्रीगुण्डिचामन्दिरमेव सत्वरं
रथाश्च गच्छन्ति सुमेरुतुल्याः।
स्वभक्तवर्गैः किल गौरचन्द्रमा
ययौ तदग्रेऽखिलभावभावितः॥१२॥

śrīguṇḍicāmandirameva satvaraṁ
rathāśca gacchanti sumerutulyāḥ|
svabhaktavargaiḥ kila gauracandramā
yayau tadagre'khilabhāvabhāvitaḥ||12||

shri-gundicha-mandiram — to the temple of Sri Gundicha; eva — indeed; satvaram — swiftly; rathah — the chariots; cha — and; gachchhanti — go; sumeru-tulyah — like Mount Sumeru; sva-bhakta-vargaih — with His throngs of devotees; kila — indeed; gaurachandrama — Gaurachandra; yayau — went; tat-agre — in front of them; akhila-bhava-bhavitah — imbued with every ecstatic feeling.

12The chariots, like Mount Sumeru, roll swiftly towards the temple of Sri Gundicha, and before them goes Gaurachandra with His devotees, imbued with every feeling of love.

Verse 13

पश्यन् जगन्नाथमुखारविन्दं
स्मरन् कुरुक्षेत्रविशालवैभवम्।
संकीर्तनानन्दसमुद्रमग्नैः
स्वभक्तवर्गैः किल वेष्टितो हरिः॥१३॥

paśyan jagannāthamukhāravindaṁ
smaran kurukṣetraviśālavaibhavam|
saṁkīrtanānandasamudramagnaiḥ
svabhaktavargaiḥ kila veṣṭito hariḥ||13||

pashyan — beholding; jagannatha-mukha-aravindam — the lotus face of Jagannatha; smaran — remembering; kurukshetra-vishala-vaibhavam — the vast splendour of Kurukshetra; sankirtana-ananda-samudra-magnaih — immersed in the ocean of the bliss of sankirtana; sva-bhakta-vargaih — by His devotees; kila — indeed; veshtitah — surrounded; harih — Hari.

13Beholding the lotus face of Jagannatha and remembering the vast splendour of Kurukshetra7, Hari went surrounded by His devotees, who were immersed in the ocean of the bliss of sankirtana.

Verse 14

श्रीराधिकाप्रेमभरातिमत्तो
हसन् रुदन् प्राह त्वमेव नाथ।
आगच्छ यामि व्रजमण्डलं विभो
वृन्दावनं यत्र सुवंशिकाध्वनिः॥१४॥

śrīrādhikāpremabharātimatto
hasan rudan prāha tvameva nātha|
āgaccha yāmi vrajamaṇḍalaṁ vibho
vṛndāvanaṁ yatra suvaṁśikādhvaniḥ||14||

shri-radhika-prema-bhara-ati-mattah — utterly intoxicated by the weight of Sri Radhika's love; hasan — laughing; rudan — weeping; praha — said; tvam eva — You; natha — O Lord; agachchha — come; yami — I go; vraja-mandalam — to Vraja-mandala; vibho — O mighty one; vrindavanam — to Vrindavana; yatra — where; su-vamshika-dhvanih — the sound of the lovely flute.

14Utterly intoxicated by the weight of Sri Radhika's love, laughing and weeping, He said, "It is You, My Lord — come! I am going to Vraja-mandala, O mighty one, to Vrindavana, where the lovely flute is sounding."

Verse 15

इति ब्रुवन् नर्तनगानमाधुरी-
समुद्रमग्नातिमनोमतङ्गजः।
श्रीगुण्डिचामन्दिरमाप सत्वरं
रथेन सार्धं जगदीश्वरस्य च॥१५॥

iti bruvan nartanagānamādhurī-
samudramagnātimanomataṅgajaḥ|
śrīguṇḍicāmandiramāpa satvaraṁ
rathena sārdhaṁ jagadīśvarasya ca||15||

iti — thus; bruvan — saying; nartana-gana-madhuri-samudra-magna-ati-mano-matangajah — the elephant of whose mind was plunged deep in the ocean of the sweetness of dance and song; shri-gundicha-mandiram — the temple of Sri Gundicha; apa — reached; satvaram — swiftly; rathena — with the chariot; sardham — together; jagat-ishvarasya — of the Lord of the world; cha — and.

15Saying this — the elephant of His mind plunged deep in the ocean of the sweetness of dance and song — He swiftly reached the temple of Sri Gundicha together with the chariot of the Lord of the world.

Verse 16

श्रीमन्दिरे रत्नमयीषु वेदीषु
स्वयंप्रकाशासु च संगतौ तौ।
विवेशतू रामजनार्दनौ सुखं
पश्यन्नति प्राह त्वमागतः किम्॥१६॥

śrīmandire ratnamayīṣu vedīṣu
svayaṁprakāśāsu ca saṁgatau tau|
viveśatū rāmajanārdanau sukhaṁ
paśyannati prāha tvamāgataḥ kim||16||

shri-mandire — in the glorious temple; ratna-mayishu — on jewelled; vedishu — altars; svayam-prakashasu — self-luminous; cha — and; samgatau — come together; tau — the two; viveshatuh — entered; rama-janardanau — Rama and Janardana; sukham — happily; pashyan — seeing (this); ati — ardently; praha — said; tvam — You; agatah — have come; kim — have.

16When Rama and Janardana, coming together, had happily entered the glorious temple and taken Their places on the jewelled, self-luminous altars, He, seeing this, ardently exclaimed, "Have You come?"

Verse 17

वृन्दावने आगत एव श्रीहरि-
रिति स्ववादीज्जनतास्वनैः प्रभुः।
सर्वं वनं रम्यमनुप्रविश्य च
स्वानन्दतृष्णोऽखिलभावपूर्णः॥१७॥

vṛndāvane āgata eva śrīhari-
riti svavādījjanatāsvanaiḥ prabhuḥ|
sarvaṁ vanaṁ ramyamanupraviśya ca
svānandatṛṣṇo'khilabhāvapūrṇaḥ||17||

vrindavane — to Vrindavana; agatah — has come; eva — truly; shri-harih — Sri Hari; iti — thus; su-avadit — proclaimed; janata-svanaih — with the cries of the crowd; prabhuh — the Lord; sarvam — the whole; vanam — garden (forest); ramyam — lovely; anupravishya — entering throughout; cha — and; sva-ananda-trishnah — thirsting for His own bliss; akhila-bhava-purnah — full of every ecstatic feeling.

17"Sri Hari has come to Vrindavana!" the Lord proclaimed aloud, echoing the cries of the crowd; and, going through the whole lovely garden, thirsting for His own bliss, He was filled with every feeling of love.

Verse 18

जगन्नाथस्य सर्वं हि भोगादिरसवैभवम्।
पश्यन् भक्तजनैः सार्धं करोति कीर्तनं महत्॥१८॥

jagannāthasya sarvaṁ hi bhogādirasavaibhavam|
paśyan bhaktajanaiḥ sārdhaṁ karoti kīrtanaṁ mahat||18||

jagannathasya — of Jagannatha; sarvam — all; hi — indeed; bhoga-adi-rasa-vaibhavam — the splendour of the rasa of the food offerings and the rest; pashyan — beholding; bhakta-janaih sardham — together with the devotees; karoti — performs; kirtanam — kirtana; mahat — great.

18Beholding all the splendour of the rasa of Jagannatha's food offerings and other services, He performs a great kirtana together with the devotees.

Verse 19

वृन्दारण्यविलासिनो मुररिपोः श्रीरासलीलां शुभां
साक्षादेव विलासलास्यलहरीपूर्णां मनन् श्रीहरिः।
श्रीराधारसमाधुरीधुरितनुर्गौराङ्गमूर्तिः स्वयं
श्रीनन्दात्मज एव भक्तिरसिकः स्वाराज्यलक्ष्मीं दधे॥१९॥

vṛndāraṇyavilāsino muraripoḥ śrīrāsalīlāṁ śubhāṁ
sākṣādeva vilāsalāsyalaharīpūrṇāṁ manan śrīhariḥ|
śrīrādhārasamādhurīdhuritanurgaurāṅgamūrtiḥ svayaṁ
śrīnandātmaja eva bhaktirasikaḥ svārājyalakṣmīṁ dadhe||19||

vrindaranya-vilasinah — who sports in Vrindaranya; mura-ripoh — of the Foe of Mura; shri-rasa-lilam — the rasa play; shubham — auspicious; sakshat eva — directly; vilasa-lasya-lahari-purnam — full of waves of play and dance; manan — regarding (it as); shri-harih — Sri Hari; shri-radha-rasa-madhuri-dhuri-tanuh — whose body bears the sweetness of Sri Radha's rasa; gauranga-murtih — in the form of Gauranga; svayam — Himself; shri-nanda-atmajah — the son of Sri Nanda; eva — truly; bhakti-rasikah — the relisher of the rasa of devotion; sva-arajya-lakshmim — the splendour of His own kingdom; dadhe — assumed.

19Regarding all this as the very rasa play, auspicious and full of waves of play and dance, of the Foe of Mura who sports in Vrindaranya, Sri Hari — the son of Sri Nanda Himself, the relisher of the rasa of devotion, in the form of Gauranga, whose body bears the sweetness of Sri Radha's rasa — assumed the splendour of His own kingdom8.

Thus ends the twentieth sarga, "The Play in the Gundicha Temple" (Shri-gundicha-mandira-vilasa), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. That is, Sri Krishna Chaitanya.
  2. The Snana-yatra: the bathing festival of Jagannatha on the full moon of the month of Jyaishtha.
  3. The anavasara: the two weeks after the Snana-yatra, when the Deities are hidden from the pilgrims' sight.
  4. Alalanatha: the Deity of Vishnu at Brahmagiri, not far from Puri.
  5. The Netrotsava ("festival of the eyes"): the day when Jagannatha appears again after the anavasara, on the eve of the Ratha-yatra.
  6. Sudarshana, the Lord's disc, worshipped on the chariot together with Subhadra.
  7. The meeting of Krishna with the people of Vraja at Kurukshetra; at the Ratha-yatra the Lord, in Radha's mood, as it were brings Krishna back from Kurukshetra to Vrindavana (the Gundicha temple).
  8. That is, Krishna Himself, having assumed in the form of Gauranga the mood and lustre of Radha, enjoys at Gundicha, as in Vrindavana, the treasure of His own abode.
